questions.q: Do you have a favourite colour?
questions.answer: I do, it's blue. I find it calming and easy on the eye, so a lot of my clothes and even my room lean towards it. It has a [[soothing]] quality that I'm naturally drawn to.

questions.q: What colours do you usually wear?
questions.answer: Mostly [[understated]] shades like navy, grey and white for everyday wear, since they look smart for work. On festival days, though, I'm happy to wear something brighter to match the mood.

questions.q: Is there a colour you don't like?
questions.answer: Not strongly, but I'm not keen on very bright orange or neon shades. They feel a bit loud and [[garish]] to me, especially on clothes, although I can see why some people love them.

questions.q: Do colours have special meanings in your country?
questions.answer: Yes, quite a few. Red and white are strongly associated with Pohela Boishakh, and the green and red of our flag are [[symbolic]] too, representing the land and the sacrifice of those who fought for independence.

questions.q: Do you think colours can affect people's mood?
questions.answer: I really believe they can. Soft blues and greens make a room feel calm, while warm colours tend to be more energising. That's probably why hospitals and offices choose their colour schemes so [[deliberately]].
